topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Language of Waves

sections.title: The Core Intuition: The 'Orchestra' Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any complex, periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves. Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of periodic functions (sin/cos). Visual: A messy, jagged wave gradually morphs as we add smooth sine waves together.
sections.example: Imagine a musician playing a chord on a piano; the ear hears one 'complex' sound, but a Fourier Series reveals the individual pure notes (frequencies) that constitute that chord.

sections.title: The Mathematical Foundation: Basis Functions
sections.content: Define the Fourier Series formula. Explain the concept of 'orthogonality'—how sine and cosine waves function like independent axes in a space. Visual: A 3D graph showing how multiple simple waves (the building blocks) align to reconstruct a square wave.
sections.example: Think of this like mixing primary colors (Red, Blue, Yellow) to paint any specific hue in a palette.

sections.title: Calculating Coefficients: The 'Sieve' Method
sections.content: Explain how we extract the amplitude of each component using integration. The integral acts as a filter that picks out specific frequencies. Visual: An animation showing a 'sieve' passing over a signal, leaving only the strength of a specific frequency component.
sections.example: Using a radio tuner: You turn the dial to 'sieve out' one specific station (frequency) from the noisy background of all radio waves in the air.

sections.title: Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave Demo
sections.content: Show the progression of adding terms: n=1, n=3, n=10. Discuss the 'Gibbs Phenomenon' (the little overshoot at corners). Visual: A growing stack of sine waves creating sharper and sharper corners of a square wave.
sections.example: A robotic cat's motion controller: Approximating a sudden jump (square wave) using smooth motor rotations to ensure the mechanical joints don't snap.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Summarize how Fourier Series transform time-domain data into frequency-domain data. Final visual: A spectrum analyzer showing real-time bars rising as an audio signal plays.
sections.example: How your smartphone compresses a high-quality song (MP3) by removing the 'inaudible' frequencies identified via the Fourier process.
